Plymouth is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable new boiler supply and installation services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Plymouth and the surrounding Devon region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional boiler installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Devon, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any new boiler supply and installation requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Plymouth with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: What is the best boiler brand?
faqs.a: Worcester Bosch, Viessmann, and Vaillant consistently top reliability surveys. All three offer extended warranties of 8-12 years when installed by accredited engineers. Brand matters less than correct sizing and installation quality.

faqs.q: Do I need to notify anyone when a new boiler is installed?
faqs.a: Yes — your Gas Safe registered installer must notify Building Control within 30 days of installation under the Competent Person Scheme. You will receive a Building Regulations completion certificate.

faqs.q: How much can a new boiler save on energy bills?
faqs.a: Replacing a G-rated boiler (pre-2005) with an A-rated condensing boiler can save £300-£500 per year on gas bills. The actual saving depends on your home size, insulation, and usage patterns.

faqs.q: Is there any financial help available for a new boiler?
faqs.a: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme offers grants of up to £7,500 for heat pump installations. The ECO4 scheme helps low-income households with free boiler replacements. Check gov.uk for current eligibility criteria.

localParagraph: Plymouth's diverse housing stock presents a range of considerations for boiler installation, from the Victorian terraces of Mutley and Stoke to the post-war semis of Plympton and the newer builds spreading across Derriford and Estover. Because Plymouth sits in an area of mixed water hardness, neither fully soft nor heavily scaled, homeowners generally benefit from a system filter and inhibitor to protect the heat exchanger and extend the boiler's working life, though the urgency varies depending on the property's existing pipework and age. Older homes in particular — particularly those with gravity-fed systems and ageing copper runs — often require additional work to bring the system up to current standards before a new condensing boiler can be fitted efficiently. Choosing a Gas Safe registered engineer familiar with Plymouth's varied property types is essential, as the correct sizing and flue route can differ significantly between a compact end-of-terrace in Greenbank and a larger detached home in Plymstock. A thorough survey before installation remains the most reliable starting point.
whatItInvolves: A new boiler installation involves removing your existing unit, upgrading the flue and pipework where required, fitting and commissioning the new boiler, and registering it with Building Control via the Competent Person Scheme. All new boiler installations must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer — it is illegal for anyone else to do this work.
process: Day 1: drain down the system, remove the old boiler, cap off existing connections. Upgrade the flue if required — most modern boilers use a concentric flue that vents through an external wall. Fit the new unit, connect flow and return pipes, gas supply, and condensate drain. Commission the boiler following manufacturer guidelines, balance the radiators, and register the installation. You'll receive a Building Regulations completion certificate within 28 days.
whatToExpect: A standard like-for-like boiler swap takes 1-2 days. A full system change — moving the boiler or converting from back boiler to combi — takes 2-4 days. Your new boiler should come with a manufacturer warranty of 5-12 years depending on brand. Always register the warranty within 30 days of installation.
